steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 2 baking sheets.

Beat applesauce, white sugar, brown sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl. In another bowl, use an electric mixer to beat egg whites until they are frothy and begin to firm up. Fold egg whites into applesauce mixture. Combine the flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon. Fold into the egg mixture. Stir in the oats, chocolate chips, walnuts, and cranberries. Drop by heaping teaspoons on prepared baking sheets.
Bake cookies in preheated oven until set and lightly browned, about 10 minutes. Remove immediately to wire racks to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Trail Mix Cookies
raw_recipe.description: There is lots of flavor in these substantial cookies filled with oats, nuts, chocolate chips, and dried fruit.

review.reviewBody: Awesome healthy cookies! These are definitely a perfect base for an "everything" cookie. These are the changes I made - partly out of necessity and partly because I am health-conscious! - I used unsweetened applesauce - Heaping 1/2 cup brown sugar only (omitted white). - 1 whole egg and 1/2 of a banana mashed - handful of sesame seeds - 1/4 cup walnuts and 1/4 sunflower seeds - 1/2 cup white and milk chocolate chips (no craisins or raisins on hand). - whole wheat flour Because I improvised a bit, I ended up having an overly sticky dough at the end so added an extra 1/4 cup of flour. I made the cookies quite large (1 1/2 dozen) and so baked them for 10 minutes. Perfect! The result is a very yummy and pretty healthy cookie - one I don't feel bad about allowing my two year old to have. Next time, I may cut the brown sugar back again to just 1/2 cup... and keep the rest of my changes :)

Love these cookies. This is the second time I made them and this time, I spiced them up. Used 2 tsp vanilla, 2 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp cloves, 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice. I didn't use chocolate chips. I substituted 1 cup of raisins. I also only used 1/2 cup of brown sugar. They were plenty sweet enough. The other spices made them taste very rich. Thanks for a great healthy cookie alternative!

these cookies are soooo wonderful!! i used cinnamon applesauce and splenda instead of the white sugar. i also made a half batch without chocolate chips for my milk-allergic daughter, so i love that this recipe doesn't include butter so she can enjoy too! i baked mine for 7 minutes and they stayed pretty soft, as we like them. they're enough to curb the sweet tooth without the major guilt trip later :)

Great starting recipe, but felt there was more to be done to make these healthier! Like other reviewers, I reduced the sugar- but mine went done to 1/4 cupe brown sugar, and 1/8 cup honey. I also increased the vanilla to 2 tsp, and salt to 1 tsp. Also used wheat flour instead of white. I love adding "extras" to my cookies, so I increased the walnuts and chocolate chips, and used raisins instead of dried cranberries. Definately a delicious alternative to regular cookies!

Based upon other reviews I adapted the recipe. Used only 1/4 cup brown sugar (no white sugar), substituted half the flour with chocolate protein powder, used one whole egg and one banana, used a combo of craisins and dried blueberries, and completely omitted the chocolate instead adding 1/2 cup mixed sunflower seeds and pumpkin seeds. Yummy! Only needed to bake for 7 minutes. Don't need the chocolate at all with all the sweetness of the fruit and the seeds really add a nice crunch. Next time would probably use less sugar. Love how they get super fluffy. Thanks for the base recipe :)

my servings where only 26 and not 36.the only change i made was,instead of 1/2 cup brown sugar i added 1/5 cup of sweetened shredded coconut cos i loooove coconut. i added the ingredients in my fitness pal and the total in calories where 94 cal per cookie.they are delicious!!!

These were the best cookies I've made in quite awhile. Used whole wheat pastry flour instead of all-purpose and only one egg. (Whipped the white and threw the yolk in with the applesauce mixture.) Cooked for exactly nine minutes. The cookies came out light and fluffy with a bit of body--very impressed. My only complaint is that to do it right takes four bowls. Thanks, dancer7899, for a great cookie recipe.

Awesome! I work-out a lot and I like to sneak in protein wherever I can so I substituted 1/2 the flour with chocolate protein powder, and also substituted the chocolate chips for unsweetened carob chips (much healthier) and only used 1/2 cup of brown sugar (no white sugar). I think next time I may try to take out the brown sugar altogether, and replace it with agave nectar or splenda. Overall, I loved these, especially the way they "fluff" up in the oven! These are my new power bar ;)

I made these in a cabin at 10,000 feet with no mixer to beat egg whites, so I used a whole egg. I had no chips, but I did have trail mix with an assortment of nuts & chips, also craisins & raisins , so I threw in a cup of that. The first sheet was cooked on an aluminum cookie sheet...they did not cook fully on the bottom. I used a baking sheet for the others...they were less gooey. Next time I will use more flour to try to remedy this. The flour I used was for high altitude baking. My husband loved these... and he is not the cookie monster I am. I will also try this at home as presented.

After going to a local cafe last week and breaking away from my usual chocolate treat,I decided to give their trail mix cookie a try. I loved it and was determined to find a recipe. I came across this one and will definitely make it again! I followed the recipe just as its given, only for my "trail mix" combo, I used shredded coconut, dried cranberries, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, and cashews. This may replace my chocolate chip cookies!
A good and easy recipe to bake. I did substitute mashed banana for the applesauce and used dark chocolate chips and the taste is pleasing!

I made this as directed except I substituted cashews for walnuts and added 1/2 c sweetened coconut. I did not find the cookies to be two sweet with the sugars and also adding in sweetened coconut. However, I think the coconut added a bit too much moisture. They still came together fine and I got rave reviews when I took them to a party, but they’re slightly on the sticky side. No mistake of the original recipe and rather my own I believe.
Used sweetened applesauce, half the amount of sugars. White morsels + cranberries + almonds is what my son likes best.

I used Splenda for the white and brown sugars which really shouldn't have changed anything, but they weren't even sweet enough for a breakfast cookie. I had to add lots more. Also, my biggest disappointment was the calories. I used a small cookie scoop that I think was the equivalent to a "heaping teaspoon" and I got five less than stated. I'm sure this sounds petty but when you are dieting every cookie counts!
these are delicious I made a few changes I omitted the white sugar and the nuts and put a banana in I also added flaxseed and used1 whole egg instead of egg white

I thought they tasted okay, but they are no bargain on calories. A Double-stuff Oreo or a fun-size Twix Cookie are less or roughly the same calorically - but, they're a little bigger and taste better.
My 'boys' love them, made two double at he's this month. I kinda change up the trail mix with what I find, raisins and craisons and chocolate chips.

I loved these and so did my kids. Subsituted pecans for walnuts and raisins for crasins. I thought they were a little sweet for my taste; may take out choc. chips and add more nuts or maybe sunflower seeds.

I only used half a cup of cane sugar and left out the brown sugar entirely. I also used pecans instead of walnuts. My dad loved them! Not too sweet, perfect as a quick snack. I will definitely be making these again.
I made these for the first time & followed the recipe exactly. I really loved how they turned out & will definitely make them again !
